newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end at one and 2-month lows.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end at one and 2-month lows.

text.p: CME hog futures fell to one-month lows and pork belly futures hit two-month lows late on expectations moderating weather will boost hog runs and slaughter rates next week, traders said.

February hogs fell to 75.650 cents late, its lowest level since December 23, and February bellies were down to 74.000, its lowest level since November 22. Both contracts finished on a weak note, they said.
Hogs closed 0.550 cent lower to unchanged with February off most at 75.750 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.750 to 0.400 lower with February off 0.675 at 74.200 cents.
Expectations that hog marketings would jump next week on moderating temperatures pressured both markets.

Cash hog prices were expected to fall $3 to $4 per cwt next week as those hogs backed up from the recent bitter cold weather are finally sent to market. A USDA report of cash pork trade at a near standstill also weighed on sentiment, traders said.
Hogs held technical support early at half way back from the recent high, but buying lacked followthrough and prices tumbled to new days lows late, they said.

Pork belly futures showed short covering support at times but retreated back to near opening lows following the lead of hog futures. Short covering from an oversold condition had offset expected pressure from increased hog runs and slaughter next week. Recent support in cash product was only coming from the weather-reduced hog kills and not from good demand for product, traders said.

The large movement of product into storage despite a lack of a hedge in futures was also considered negative. Recent stepped-up storings should also offset any friendly ideas on next week's USDA monthly Cold Storage report, they said.

Analyst estimates on the report pointed to total U.S. frozen belly stocks at between 37.4 to 41.5 million lbs. This compares with 30.9 million on hand December 1 and 47.6 million in storage January 1, 1996.
Both markets closed early at noon CST ahead of the Martin Luther King Jr holiday on Monday. Markets will close early at noon on Monday.
